definitions.explanation: Able to withstand wear, pressure, or damage; not easily broken.
Having good health, not prone to illness.

examples.japanese: この{机|つくえ}は{丈夫|じょうぶ}です。
{丈夫|じょうぶ}な{体|からだ}を{作|つく}りましょう。
おじいさんは{丈夫|じょうぶ}ですね。
{丈夫|じょうぶ}な{靴|くつ}を{買|か}いたい。
examples.english: I want to buy sturdy shoes.

examples.japanese: この{鞄|かばん}は{見|み}た{目|め}より{丈夫|じょうぶ}で、{十年|じゅうねん}も{使|つか}っています。
examples.english: This bag is sturdier than it looks, and I've been using it for ten years.
examples.notes: Longer example showing durability over time

notes:
{丈夫|じょうぶ} is a na-adjective: {丈夫|じょうぶ}な (before nouns), {丈夫|じょうぶ}だ/です (predicate). It can describe both objects (sturdy/durable) and people (healthy).

Note: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ} (all right, okay) is a related word. The kanji {丈|じょう} means 'length/height' and {夫|ふ} means 'man' - originally referring to a grown, strong man.
